_sources.title: Trenggiling Masuk Pemukiman di Banjarbaru, Korban Karhutla?

1.why: Speed is defined as the distance traveled divided by the time taken.

wrong.a: Multiplying distance by time does not give speed.
wrong.c: Time divided by distance is the inverse of speed.
wrong.d: Multiplying mass by speed is momentum.

2.why: 900 metres divided by 1,800 seconds equals 0.50 metres per second.

wrong.c: 1,800 m/s is much too fast for an animal.
wrong.d: 0.02 m/s is too slow for this calculation.

3.why: Forest fires and smoke destroy natural habitats, forcing animals to flee into residential areas [1].

wrong.a: Animals do not visit city parks for leisure.
wrong.b: Animals do not seek out cars.
wrong.d: Animals do not swim in city swimming pools.

_quiz_pool.question: What is the standard unit of speed?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Speed is measured in metres per second.

_quiz_pool.question: If you double the distance while time stays the same, speed...
_quiz_pool.explanation: Speed is directly proportional to distance.

Why did wildlife rescuers step in during the Banjarbaru fires?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Rescuers helped animals that fled from burnt forests into neighborhoods [1].

_quiz_pool.question: Which animal was rescued in Banjarbaru weighing 9 kg?
_quiz_pool.explanation: A 9 kg Sunda pangolin was rescued from a drainage ditch [1].

story.title: The pangolin's journey
story.lead: Wildfires and land clearing filled parts of South Kalimantan with smoke [1]. A 9-kilogram Sunda pangolin was rescued after entering a city residential drainage channel [1].

story.body_1: Forest fires destroy vegetation, logs, and insect nests that animals rely on for food [1]. When smoke and heat damage their habitat, creatures like pangolins, lizards, and civets must move to survive [1].
story.body_2: Wildlife rescuers in Banjarbaru noted an increase in animals leaving burnt lands for urban edges [1], while meteorological data tracks dry conditions [2].
timeline.1.text: Pangolins forage safely inside dense forest habitats [1].
timeline.2.text: Smoke and flames force animals to flee toward safer grounds [1].
timeline.3.text: Exhausted animals wander into urban residential areas [1].
physics.title: Calculating travel speed
physics.body_1: When animals travel to escape danger, speed tells us how fast they move across the ground. Speed is the distance covered divided by the time taken [1].
physics.body_2: The formula is v = s ÷ t. If an animal travels a certain distance in a given time, its average speed is easy to find [1].
physics.assumptions: We assume steady movement along a straight path from the forest edge to the rescue site.

lab.title: Mini Lab: Measuring Walking Speed
lab.step_1: Mark a 10-metre straight line outdoors or in a hallway using chalk or tape.
lab.step_2: Walk normally along the line while a friend times you with a stopwatch.
lab.step_3: Calculate your speed by dividing distance by time (v = s ÷ t).
lab.question: What was your walking speed in m/s, and how does it compare to animal escape speeds?
